intro: User-Managed Access 2.0, one authorization server per trust realm. A resource server registers a resource owner's resources with a protection API access token (PAT), asks for a permission ticket when a client arrives without access, and the client trades the ticket for a requesting party token (RPT) at the token endpoint. Every permission in an RPT is decided by the realm's uma-authorization policy, then by the owner's own document.
turnedOff: UMA is turned off in this realm (uma.enabled): its endpoints answer 404 and the uma-ticket grant is not offered.
noEndpoints: No endpoints while UMA is turned off.
serversLead: The applications declared for uma. A resource server's PAT needs the delegated permission grant of urn:sts:uma-protection-api:uma_protection; an application that may own resources registers its own, with a PAT it obtained as itself.
noServers: No application is declared for uma in this realm.
enableLabel: Make an application a resource server:
ticketsLead: Live tickets, by the first characters of a hash of each: a ticket is a bearer artifact and is never shown.
pendingLead: Requests a client submitted with request_submitted, waiting for the resource owner to approve or refuse. A person answers on /portal/shared; an application that owns resources is answered on its owner tab.
ownerLead: One owner's resources, document and waiting requests. A person's document is read here and edited only by them; an application that owns resources has its document edited here, by administrators and by the application's owners.
ownerNotFound: There is no person or application "{owner}" in this realm.
personReadOnly: A person's document is theirs: they edit it on /portal/shared.
notOwning: This application does not carry umaOwnsResources TRUE, so it has no document of its own.
whatIfLead: What the token endpoint would answer for one permission, every layer: the realm's policy, the owner's document and the resource server's fine-grained policy. Asked as a dry run, neither audited nor counted.
whatIfProblem: That cannot be asked: check the {which}.
